summary: The City Council passed several measures on September 15, 2023 to modernize local traffic regulations, effective by November 1st, aiming to improve road safety, cut commute times, and promote eco-friendly transport. Key changes include AI smart traffic signals, safety enhancements, the Green Lane Project for cycling, and increased bus funding. Residents voice support, and the Council plans town halls and future steps like EV charging and possible congestion pricing.
one_line: The City Council passed traffic reforms on September 15, 2023, adding smart signals, bus lanes, bike infrastructure and safety measures, effective November 1st.
key_facts: The City Council passed the traffic measures on September 15, 2023, and they are expected to take effect by November 1st.
Councilmember Kimberly Sanchez spearheaded the campaign for updated traffic laws, saying "Our streets should be avenues of connectivity, not zones of chaos."
The revisions include dedicated bus lanes on major thoroughfares, expanded cycling infrastructure, and smart traffic signals that adapt in real time.
Smart traffic lights use AI technology to respond to real-time traffic patterns, reducing stoppage and idling and curbing vehicle emissions.
Local tech startup GreenLight Innovations was awarded the contract to install the smart signals.
Safety initiatives include widening sidewalks, restricting heavy trucks to night-time travel, and low-speed zones around schools and parks.
The Green Lane Project will expand bike lanes and provide more secure bicycle parking.
The Council announced significant funding increases for the public bus system, including upgraded buses with Wi-Fi and real-time tracking, to reduce headways and improve reliability.
Town hall meetings and informational workshops are slated for late September to address concerns and educate the public.
Alex Rodriguez, a local graphic designer, switched to cycling after the Green Lane Project and finds it faster than driving during rush hour.
Sara Jenkins, a project manager, started taking the bus thanks to improved services and reports lower daily stress.
Future plans include evaluating the regulations' impact, expanding electric vehicle charging stations, and possibly introducing congestion pricing.
